I'm currently open to new opportunities as a Senior Data Engineer or Data Platform Lead, with a focus on healthcare and biotech industries.

As a seasoned data engineer with hands-on experience in PySpark, I wanted to share a crucial lesson I've learned from optimizing Spark execution plans. When working with large-scale data processing, understanding how Spark executes your code can make all the difference.

Recently, I worked on a project where I had to optimize a slow-running PySpark job. Using the `.explain()` method, I generated a detailed execution plan, which revealed a bottleneck in the shuffle phase. By adjusting the `spark.shuffle.compress` and `spark.shuffle.spill.compress` configurations, I was able to reduce the job's runtime by 30%.

Another key optimization was reordering the operations to minimize data serialization and deserialization. For instance, applying `.filter()` before `.join()` significantly reduced the amount of data being shuffled.

If you're looking for a data engineer who can dive deep into Spark execution plans and optimize performance, I'd love to connect. Let's discuss how my expertise can help drive efficiency in your healthcare or biotech organization's data platform.
